analysis.note: Proper name; nominative subject of the first uvāca, the reporting formula.
Accusative masculine singular; the person addressed by Madhusūdana, qualified by the following accusative masculine participles/adjective-compound.
Instrumental of cause/means with āviṣṭam: “by/with compassion.”
Past passive participial adjective from ā + √viś, “entered, possessed, overcome”; agrees with tam.

samasa.vigraha: aśrubhiḥ pūrṇe ākule ca īkṣaṇe yasya

analysis.note: Masculine accusative singular bahuvrīhi agreeing with tam; the final member īkṣaṇa is “eye/sight,” while the whole compound denotes the person possessing such eyes. Internal sandhi: ākula + īkṣaṇa → ākulekṣaṇa.

verification.detail: compound stem aśrupūrṇākulekṣaṇa as Pum/Dvitiya/Eka: pass; relation bahuvrihi: unsupported (logged)

analysis.note: Present active participial adjective from vi + √sad, “desponding, sinking in dejection”; agrees with tam. Stem recorded as viṣīdant, since the accusative singular form is viṣīdantam, not viṣīdatam.
Neuter accusative singular, agreeing with vākyam as the speech-object of the second uvāca.
Neuter accusative singular object: the utterance spoken.
Perfect used narratively: “said/spoke.” This is the main reported action within Saṃjaya’s frame.
Nominative subject of the second uvāca; an epithet of Kṛṣṇa, “slayer of Madhu.”

verification.detail: compound stem madhusūdana as Pum/Prathama/Eka: pass; relation tatpurusa: unsupported (logged)

justifications.decision: The accusative tam, with āviṣṭam, aśrupūrṇākulekṣaṇam, and viṣīdantam agreeing with it, is construed with the second uvāca; idam vākyam is the speech-object of that same verb, and madhusūdanaḥ is its nominative subject.
options_considered: Take Saṃjaya as the subject of the whole sentence addressing tam directly.
Take the first uvāca as a frame and the second uvāca with madhusūdanaḥ as the main reported action.
justifications.chosen: saṃjayaḥ uvāca is the reporting frame, while madhusūdanaḥ uvāca idam vākyam tam ... is the reported action: “Sañjaya said: … Madhusūdana spoke this utterance to him ….”

justifications.decision: The instrumental kṛpayā is best taken as the cause or possessing force with the past passive participle āviṣṭam from ā + √viś, whose lexical range includes “enter” and “take possession of.”
options_considered: Idiomatic passive/resultative: “possessed or overcome by compassion.”

justifications.decision: Although the final member īkṣaṇa is neuter, the compound as a whole agrees with tam in masculine accusative singular; therefore it describes the person, not an independent neuter object “eye.”
options_considered: A neuter accusative object: “a tear-filled, troubled eye/sight.”
A bahuvrīhi adjective qualifying tam: “whose eyes were tear-filled and troubled.”
justifications.chosen: aśrupūrṇākulekṣaṇam is a masculine accusative singular bahuvrīhi: “having eyes filled with tears and troubled.”

justifications.decision: The form is a present active participle from vi + √sad, agreeing with tam; its aspect is simultaneous with Madhusūdana’s speaking, not a separate finite action.
options_considered: Treat it as a finite verb: “he desponded.”
Treat it as a participial qualifier: “desponding.”

justifications.decision: In this epic context the compound madhu-sūdana is the proper epithet of Viṣṇu-Kṛṣṇa, not the alternative lexical sense “bee” or the literal “destroyer of honey.”
options_considered: Contextual epic epithet: “Madhusūdana, slayer of Madhu.”
justifications.chosen: madhusūdanaḥ is Kṛṣṇa’s epithet, “slayer of Madhu.”

translation:
Sañjaya said:
To him—thus overcome by compassion, with eyes filled with tears and troubled, desponding—Madhusūdana (slayer of Madhu) spoke this utterance.
one_shot_delta: A commentary-blind or syntax-blind translation might make Saṃjaya the speaker to Arjuna, missing that Saṃjaya is only framing Madhusūdana’s speech.
It might treat aśrupūrṇākulekṣaṇam as an independent neuter object, rather than as a masculine accusative bahuvrīhi qualifying tam.
It might render kṛpayā āviṣṭam too literally as “entered by compassion,” instead of the idiom “overcome/possessed by compassion.”
It might choose the non-contextual meaning of madhusūdana, such as “bee” or “destroyer of honey,” rather than Kṛṣṇa’s epithet “slayer of Madhu.”
analyzer_disagreements: ByT5 gives āviṣṭam and viṣīdantam under verbal/root lemmas (āviś, viṣad). Under the requested format they are treated as subanta participial adjectives, so the lemmas are recorded as nominal stems āviṣṭa and viṣīdant, with derivational notes preserving ā + √viś and vi + √sad.
ByT5 locally splits aśru_pūrṇa_ākula_īkṣaṇam into member analyses. Since the printed unit is one compound word, it is recorded here as a single bahuvrīhi compound with those members.
Corrected after verifier report: viṣīdantam is not derived from a nominal stem viṣīdat as claimed before, since that yields viṣīdatam; the stem is recorded as viṣīdant.
mula: saṃjaya uvāca taṃ tathā kṛpayāviṣṭam aśrupūrṇākulekṣaṇam | viṣīdantam idaṃ vākyam uvāca madhusūdanaḥ
